analysis:
The only changed file is CHANGELOG.md, which was reviewed in full. The diff is documentation-only. It adds a v0.9.21 candidate section. The new Fixed entry says one-token startup health-check timings are kept out of serving throughput estimates. It also says supported loaded models are bootstrapped with bounded, preemptible measurements. The diff also relabels v0.9.20 as dated 2026-10-12 and rewords its release-identity bullet. No source, protocol, key-handling, attestation, encryption, authorization or billing code is in this change. The changelog itself does not alter any threat-model control, so there are no regressions against T-041 (the SSD cache) or against TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011.

One point for later passes: the v0.9.21 bullet describes provider behavior (throughput estimates and bootstrap measurements). Its implementing source changes are not in this batch. If that implementation ships separately, reviewers should check two things. First, that the bootstrap measurements use no real consumer prompts and no cache-visible or cross-tenant content. Second, that they do not skew routing or throughput claims in ways a malicious provider could exploit. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a problem.
